summary: Timeboxed join access request: prod inference traces + payment connector logs to investigate customer billing mismatch
description:
Issue summary:
A product team reported a billing mismatch for a single enterprise customer (Acme Payments) where token counts returned by the hosted API did not align with the customer's invoiced usage for a 6-hour window on 2026-03-08. The investigator needs to join raw inference traces with payment connector logs to attribute requests to invoices and validate whether a connector retry loop inflated reported tokens.

Impact:
- Potential overbilling for a single enterprise customer (financial + reputational risk).
- Affects invoiced usage reconciliation for March billing period.

Environment:
- Production, us-east region (us-east-1).
- Models in scope: redwood-instruct-13b serving in hosted API fleet.

Requested access:
- Timeboxed, read-only join query across: production inference traces (raw requests/response token counts, request_ids, session_ids), and payments connector ingestion logs (connector retries, invoice attribution records) for window 2026-03-08T02:00:00Z to 2026-03-08T08:00:00Z.
- Export format: anonymized CSV with hashed customer identifiers (SHA256 salt stored in vault) and redaction of any user-submitted prompt content; retain only token counts, request/response metadata, timestamps, connector status codes, and mapping keys.
- Purpose: reproduce mismatch and confirm whether a connector retry or double-ingestion caused inflated token accounting.

Steps to reproduce (investigator playbook):
1) Query inference traces for request_ids in time window and extract token_count_out, token_count_in, model_version, route_id, session_id.
2) Query payments connector logs for the same window for events labeled invoice_emit, connector_retry, inbound_webhook_receive; map to request/session identifiers via mapping table.
3) Perform inner join on mapping key to compare token attribution vs. invoiced entries.
4) Produce anonymized summary and a minimal sample of raw rows ( <= 25 rows) with redaction for legal/security verification.

Compliance rationale and safeguards requested:
- Timeboxed access for 48 hours from approval timestamp.
- Redaction: drop free-text prompt/response fields entirely; keep only numeric counters and opaque IDs.
- Access via bastion with session recording enabled; actions audited and logged.
- Investigator agrees to purge local copies after verification; verification evidence to be uploaded to Confluence.

Expected outputs:
- Repro steps and proof of whether double-ingest occurred.
- If overbilling confirmed: list of affected invoice IDs and suggested remediation steps.

Requesting team: Billing Ops / Prod Support (contact: Carlos Mendes).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Initial triage by Billing Ops found a cluster of invoices with token_count > expected for Acme Payments between 02:00-08:00 UTC on 2026-03-08.
Hypothesis A: payments connector retried ingestion leading to duplicate invoice rows (connector_retry observed in connector logs).
Hypothesis B: serving runtime replayed requests due to transient 502s, causing duplicate downstream accounting events.
Needed artifacts: mapping table (session_id -> customer_hash), raw trace storage prefix: s3://redwood-prod/traces/2026/03/08/us-east/, payments logs prefix: gs://connectors/prod/us-east/2026/03/08/.
Security note: prompts and responses must not be exported; confirm query omits 'payload' and 'response_text' fields.
comments: Aisha Patel (reporter) - 2026-03-10: Raised request after customer-facing billing ops escalated. Asking for timeboxed join to validate invoice deltas.
Riley Zhang (assignee) - 2026-03-10: Acknowledged. Preparing access request to SecOps and Compliance. Will need explicit redaction plan and JIT access window.

Carlos Mendes (Billing Ops) - 2026-03-11: Performed join and confirmed pattern consistent with connector retries; provided preliminary list of candidate invoice_ids to Security for remediation steps.

resolution_notes: Access approved by SecOps/Compliance with strong conditions. Investigation confirmed duplicated ingestion events caused by a bug in the payments connector retry logic. Remediation: roll forward fix in connectors service (PR https://github.com/redwood/connectors/pull/1457) and issue credit to Acme Payments for affected invoices. Billing Ops to create SUP ticket to contact customer and process credit. Postmortem scheduled and link will be attached.
audit_requirements: Session recordings retained; IAM role creation logged; Confluence upload with investigator attestation required. Compliance to verify purge of exports after 7 days. Security to archive access artifact to vault for future audits.
follow_up_tasks: Billing Ops: open customer-facing SUP ticket to notify Acme Payments and process credit (assigned to Carlos Mendes).
Infra: deploy connectors hotfix and monitor for duplicate ingestion for next 72 hours (assigned to infra oncall).
DevRel: prepare short communication for affected customers if more are identified (owner: Priya Rao).
Compliance: confirm purge of any extracted datasets and close internal access after verification (owner: Maya Singh).
